card.title: Senior Manager of Production
card.description:
Gwynedd Manufacturing is seeking a hands-on Senior Manager of Production with a strong CNC machining background to lead day-to-day operations in a high-precision environment. This role is ideal for someone who has progressed through the ranks—from the shop floor into leadership—and is ready to step into a broader operational role.

The ideal candidate brings deep, practical knowledge of CNC machining (mills, lathes, EDM) and thrives in a fast-paced, high-tolerance manufacturing setting. This is not a purely strategic role—this leader will be actively engaged on the floor, driving performance, mentoring teams, and continuously improving processes.

Key Responsibilities:

* Lead daily plant operations with a strong presence on the manufacturing floor, ensuring output, quality, and efficiency targets are met
* Direct oversight of machining operations including CNC mills, lathes, and EDM, ensuring optimal machine utilization and performance
* Manage and develop a team of supervisors, leads, and machinists (50–100+ employees)
* Serve as a technical resource and mentor, supporting setup, programming, and troubleshooting when needed
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, scrap reduction, and process standardization
* Partner closely with Engineering and Quality to ensure tight tolerance requirements and manufacturability of parts
* Own production scheduling, workflow optimization, and labor planning to meet customer demand
* Establish and reinforce shop floor accountability, KPIs, and standard work practices
* Maintain a safe, compliant, and disciplined manufacturing environment
* Support new product introductions and prototype builds with a strong understanding of machining constraints
* Overseeing multiple departments withing the manufacturing space.

Qualifications:

* 5+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with clear growth from hands-on machining into leadership
* Strong CNC background required (setup, programming, and/or machining experience with mills, lathes, EDM)
* Prior experience in roles such as Machine Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, or Plant Manager
* Proven ability to lead teams in a high-precision, tight-tolerance environment
* Deep understanding of machining processes, tooling, fixturing, and production workflows
* Experience driving continuous improvement on the shop floor (Lean, process optimization, etc.)
* Comfortable being hands-on and highly visible in daily operations, not just managing from an office
* Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to develop talent from within
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field preferred, but equivalent hands-on experience strongly valued

Physical and Work Environment Requirements: 
This position is based in a manufacturing environment and may require the following over extended periods of time up to a full 8-hour work shift (excluding lunch and breaks): stand, walk, sit, squat or bend, kneel and rise, lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to — and occasionally exceeding — 50 pounds, view a computer or other digital screen, work on a computer, workstation or comparable system, and make accurate entries in such systems. Manual dexterity and fine motor skills are required for detailed assembly and precision work. Work may take place in areas with varying temperatures or no climate control, varying noise levels, and production equipment in motion. Proper personal protective equipment (PPE) must be worn in designated areas at all times as required by company policy. Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals with disabilities but are always subject to safety concerns for the employee and all team members. Employer may require a physical assessment of the candidate’s ability to perform these tasks as a condition of an offer letter. Any assessment will be performed by a third party vendor and will be reported on a pass/fail basis with no other medical information conveyed to employer.

*Equal Opportunity Employer:* 
*Gwynedd Manufacturing is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.*

*Note: This job description reflects general duties and responsibilities and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Management may modify or assign other responsibilities as needed.*

card.title: Director, Quality Performance Operations
card.description:
**Company****:**
================

AHI agilon health, inc.

**Job Posting Location****:**
=============================

Remote - USA

**Job Title****:**
==================

Director, Quality Performance Operations

**Job Description****:**
========================

***Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.***

The Director, Quality Operations is a hands-on, results-driven operator responsible for disciplined, scalable execution across HEDIS, Stars, clinical quality programs, and the In-Home Assessment (IHA) program. Reporting to the Senior Director, Quality, this role provides operational leadership for the Quality Operations team and directly oversees the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations. The Director serves as the critical connection point between the centralized operations team and regional and market teams, between operations and technology, and alongside the Payor team with our health plan partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, and work gets done. This role is built for a strong operator with a bias for action: someone who brings structure to complexity, holds teams and partners accountable, closes loops, and consistently delivers measurable improvement in quality results.

**Essential Job Function**s:

**1. Operational Leadership and Execution**

Lead the day-to-day operating model for enterprise quality programs, including HEDIS, Stars, ACO/MSSP quality initiatives, clinical quality programs, and the IHA program.

Execute priorities set by the Senior Director through annual operating plans, workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Directly manage and develop the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations, and provide leadership across the broader quality operations team.

Serve as the primary liaison between the centralized Quality Operations team and regional and market teams, ensuring enterprise priorities, workflows, and expectations are clearly communicated, adopted, and executed locally, and that market needs, barriers, and feedback are surfaced and resolved centrally.

Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence, including action-item tracking, issue logs, escalation paths, and KPI scorecards, so that commitments are owned, deadlines are met, and open items are driven to closure.

**2. IHA Program Oversig**ht

Own end-to-end operational oversight of the IHA program, including implementation planning, workflow design, market readiness, vendor coordination, KPI monitoring, and issue resolution.

Partner with market, clinical, analytics, coding, risk adjustment, and health plan teams to ensure IHA activities support quality and clinical objectives.

Monitor IHA program productivity, completion, quality, member experience, documentation, and downstream outcomes; implement corrective actions when results are below target.

Drive consistent IHA execution across regions and markets, holding vendors and internal partners accountable to targets and ensuring identified gaps and follow-up needs are closed.

**3. Quality Program Operation**s

Ensure operational readiness for HEDIS/Stars submissions, audits, roadmaps and health plan deliverables.

Coordinate enterprise and market-level quality calendars, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across cross-functional teams.

Drive continuous improvement by evaluating workflows, identifying root causes, and implementing scalable solutions.

**4. Technology Partnership and Prioritizatio**n

Serve as the liaison between Quality Operations and the Technology and Product teams, translating operational needs into clearly defined business requirements, use cases, and success measures.

Lead prioritization of quality-related technology requests and enhancements based on quality impact, operational risk, and timing; maintain a transparent backlog and roadmap in partnership with Technology.

Track delivery of technology work against committed timelines, coordinate user acceptance testing and rollout with operations and market users, and escalate risks or delays as needed.

**5. Health Plan Partnershi**p

Work alongside the Payor team to track, manage, and follow up on open health plan items, requests, and deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution.

Attend and actively participate in health plan meetings, including Joint Operating Committees (JOCs) and quality working sessions, to build strong partnerships with health plan partners and drive quality results.

Lead operational discussions with health plans on quality programs, data exchange and supplemental data, gap closure, and quality results; ensure action items from health plan meetings are documented and completed.

Maintain a consolidated view of health plan quality commitments, programs, and incentive opportunities across markets to inform prioritization and resource planning.

**6. Stakeholder and Vendor Managemen**t

Build collaborative relationships with Regional Quality, Market, Payor, Clinical, Analytics, Coding, Risk Adjustment, Technology, Product, Finance, and other enterprise partners.

Lead operational discussions with vendors and external partners; monitor results against service levels, quality standards, and contractual commitments.

Support materials and deliverables for executive, Board, JOC, CQC, and other governance forums as requested.

**Other Job Functions:**

* Understand, adhere to, and implement the Company’s policies and procedures.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and mentoring to employees and team members.
* Support hiring, employee reviews, workforce planning, and development activities for the function.
* Demonstrate excellent communication, customer service, attention to detail, and accountability.
* Travel as required.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

**Minimum Experience**

* Minimum of 9 years of applicable healthcare quality, clinical operations, or program operations experience, including at least 3 years of people management experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional quality programs in Medicare Advantage, value-based care, HEDIS/Stars, ACO/MSSP, or a comparable environment.
* Experience overseeing large-scale operational programs, vendors, KPI tracking, and process improvement; IHA or in-home clinical program experience strongly preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS, CMS and NCQA requirements, quality measurement, and healthcare operations.
* Proven track record as a strong, hands-on operator who drives execution, holds teams and partners accountable, and delivers results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
* Experience partnering directly with health plans (e.g., JOCs, quality program partnerships) and with technology teams on requirements and prioritization strongly preferred.

**2. Education/Licensure:**

Bachelor’s degree required in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, business, data analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred

**Skills and Abilities**:

1. Strong operator with a bias for action; able to take ambiguous problems, build a plan, and drive them to completion

2. Ability to manage multiple priorities, workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously with minimal supervision

3. Skilled at influencing and aligning cross-functional, regional, market, and external stakeholders without direct authority

4. Ability to translate operational needs into clear technology requirements and priorities

5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills; uses data to monitor results and drive decisions

6. Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through; ensures open items are tracked and closed

7. Language Skills: Strong communication skills both written and verbal to work with multiple internal and external clients in a fast-paced environment

8. Mathematical Skills: Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

9. Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.

10. Computer Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); experience with project and work management tools preferred

**Essential Physical Functions**:

These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all the functions of the job with or without accommodation.

 
 
 
 

**Location****:**
=================

Remote - GA

**Pay Range****:**
==================

$129,700.00 - $162,100.00

Salary range shown is a guideline. Individual compensation packages can vary based on factors unique to each candidate, such as skill set, experience, and qualifications.

card.description:
*Reports To: SVP and General Manager, Business Operations*

**About Luminary Hospice:**
---------------------------

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

### **About the role:**

The Director of Quality is responsible for leading, designing, and continuously improving the organization's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. This role ensures compliance with all federal, state, and accrediting body requirements while driving a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality patient care. The Director of Quality partners closely with clinical, operational, and executive leadership to translate quality data into meaningful improvements that enhance patient outcomes, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

This leader serves as the organization's subject-matter expert on quality, survey preparedness, and performance improvement, balancing regulatory rigor with practical, frontline-focused solutions.

**Job Responsibilities**

**Quality & Performance Improvement**

* Lead and oversee the organization's QAPI program, ensuring alignment with CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulations, and accreditation standards.

* Develop, implement, and monitor performance improvement initiatives based on data trends, adverse events, and regulatory requirements.

* Analyze quality metrics, patient outcomes, and incident reports to identify risks, root causes, and opportunities for improvement.

* Ensure corrective action plans are developed, implemented, and sustained across departments and markets. (Let's discuss with Nicole)

**Regulatory Compliance & Survey Readiness**

* Serve as the primary owner of regulatory readiness, including CMS, state surveys, and accrediting body reviews.

* Lead mock surveys, tracer activities, and ongoing readiness assessments to ensure continuous compliance.

* Coordinate survey responses, plans of correction, and follow-up activities in partnership with agency leadership.

* Stay current on regulatory changes and proactively educate leaders on impact and expectations.

**Patient Safety & Risk Management**

* Oversee patient safety initiatives, including incident reporting, investigations, and follow-up actions.

* Lead root cause analyses (RCAs) and failure mode assessments as needed.

* Partner with clinical leadership to reduce risk, prevent harm, and improve safety outcomes for patients and staff.

**Data, Reporting & Insights**

* Develop and maintain quality dashboards and reports for executive leadership, agency leaders, and governing bodies.

* Translate complex quality and compliance data into clear, actionable insights.

* Ensure accurate and timely reporting of required quality measures and outcomes.

**Leadership, Education & Collaboration**

* Partner with Executive Directors, Clinical Leaders, and Medical Directors to embed quality expectations into daily operations.

* Educate and coach leaders and frontline staff on quality standards, best practices, and regulatory requirements.

* Support a culture of transparency, continuous learning, and accountability.

* Participate in leadership meetings and provide strategic guidance on quality-related decisions.

**Job Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse (RN) with active, unrestricted license

* Minimum 5 years of hospice or home health experience

* Minimum 3 years in quality, compliance, or clinical leadership

* Strong knowledge of CMS Hospice Conditions of Participation

* Experience with surveys and regulatory audits

* Strong analytical and communication skills

**Preferred**

* Hospice or quality certification (CHPN, CPHQ, or similar)

* Experience with accreditation organizations (CHAP, ACHC, Joint Commission)

### **Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit or stand. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity:**

Luminary Hospice is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination and harassment, where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. All employment decisions at Luminary Hospice are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.

### **Compensation and Benefits:**

Luminary Hospice offers a competitive compensation package, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings options, and more. Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term financial goals.

Director-Quality Management - Acute | Highland Hospital | Charleston, West Virginia

**About the Job:**

PURPOSE STATEMENT: 
 
The Director of Quality, Risk & Compliance leads and coordinates quality and performance improvement, regulatory compliance, and patient safety efforts within the healthcare facility. This role ensures that all programs operate within local, state, federal, and accreditation standards, while driving a culture of continuous improvement, clinical excellence, and risk reduction.

**Roles and Responsibilities:**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Provides oversight of all facility programs, including inpatient and outpatient services, ensuring alignment with quality, risk management, patient safety, and regulatory standards.
* Leads facility-wide quality, risk, and patient safety strategy and improvement efforts.
* Directs the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, including development, implementation, and evaluation; monitors KPIs and ensures governance of data-driven improvement efforts.
* Drives organization-wide performance improvement initiatives through data analysis and system-level process enhancements to improve outcomes.
* Oversees incident reporting, investigations, and risk analyses (RCA/Event Analysis), ensuring timely resolution and prevention of recurrence.
* Maintains compliance with all local, state, federal (CMS), and accreditation standards (TJC), ensures ongoing survey readiness, and serves as the primary liaison during regulatory and accreditation surveys, audits, and required reporting activities.
* Partners with the Legal, Compliance, and Risk Department on high-risk events, complaints/allegations, investigations, and corrective action planning.
* Supports the development, review, and implementation of facility policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and consistent adherence across departments.
* Collaborates with department leaders and Human Resources to support staff accountability and ensure adherence to facility policies and procedures.
* Provides staff training and mentoring to support competency, accountability, and adherence to quality, risk, and safety standards, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and patient safety.
* Conducts leadership rounding, medical record reviews, and monitoring of environment of care, safety, and documentation standards.
* Prepares and maintains required reports and documentation; participates in committees, meetings, audits, and organizational initiatives.
* Supervises Patient Advocate/Coordinator roles, when applicable, through hiring, orienting, performance assessment and management, motivating, training, scheduling, and coaching to meet department and facility goals. Supports resolution of patient concerns and patient rights processes.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of patient safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of client safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.

**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) environment.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable. Direct leadership of quality teams is preferred.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

* Develop quality objectives, metrics, and management-review processes.
* Ensure QMS processes are understood, implemented, and effective across the organization.
* Identify gaps, risks, and opportunities for improvement and develop practical plans to address them.
